brief:
Palestinian citizens of Israel face a stark choice between abstaining from voting and participating in an election system they perceive as structurally stacked against their interests, Al Jazeera English reported. With the race at a knife's edge, many weigh whether principle or strategic voting serves their community better in a political landscape that limits their power.

The dilemma reflects broader disillusionment among Palestinian voters who question whether engagement in Israeli electoral politics can meaningfully advance their rights and concerns. For some, casting a ballot represents tacit acceptance of a system they view as fundamentally inequitable; for others, boycotting the vote amounts to surrendering what little leverage they possess.
dek: With vote at knife’s edge, Palestinian citizens weigh principle against strategic voting in system stacked against them.
title: Palestinian citizens navigate fear and apathy in Israeli election
